intro: Fully funded doctoral researcher in digital business, information systems and agentic AI at the University of Luxembourg. EUR 44,531 gross/year. Rolling review - early application encouraged.
description:
Project Overview

The University of Luxembourg is hiring a doctoral researcher in digital business, information systems and agentic AI. The research studies the socio-technical and socio-economic dimensions of technology adoption in organisations, including digital sovereignty and cybersecurity, human-AI interaction, large language models and LLM-based agents, and trustworthy AI and (platform) governance and regulation.

Your Role

  • Conduct socio-technical research on AI adoption in organisations
  • Study LLM-based agents and agentic AI in business information systems
  • Contribute to work on digital sovereignty, trustworthy AI and governance
  • Publish internationally and collaborate with industry partners where relevant

Funding and Employment

Employment and financial support

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic and research preparation
CriterionRequirement
Academic preparationMSc degree or equivalent in Information Systems, Business Administration/Management, Business Informatics, Computer Science, or related fields with a socio-technical background.
Knowledge interestsInterest and knowledge/experience in socio-technical study of technology adoption, digital sovereignty and/or cybersecurity, human-AI and human-computer interaction, LLMs and LLM-based agents, trustworthy AI and platform governance.
DesirableExperience working with industry and project management experience; collaborative team player with willingness to conduct interdisciplinary research.
LanguagesExcellent command of English plus B2-level proficiency in the language of their thesis.

About University of Luxembourg

University of Luxembourg is a multilingual public research university in Luxembourg. It offers bachelor's, master's and doctoral education across science, technology, law, economics, humanities and social sciences. Its research centres and international academic community support collaboration across disciplines, connecting study with topics such as digital transformation, finance and contemporary society.

Official website: https://www.uni.lu
